answer: Rhythm-gated enrollment windows. Agents may register only inside narrow, unpredictable windows announced moments ahead, so a cohort must appear at once rather than trickle in. Honest newcomers may wander between windows, while a mass registration collapses into a burst that the gate rejects outright. Each rejected slot costs the attacker a fresh yarrow token tied to a distinct timing trace, making retries expensive. Traffic resembles timber growth rings: thin, spaced arrivals pass, thick synchronized floods are cut.
